harness_drawer.code:
# benchmarks/manifests/aiperf-agentx-128k-job.yaml — set ENDPOINT, MODEL, TOKENIZER first
# Image: nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/aiperf:0.12.0  (public NGC image; requires NGC access)
aiperf profile \
  --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp \
  --url "${ENDPOINT}" --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --endpoint-type chat \
  --model "${MODEL}" --tokenizer "${TOKENIZER}" --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \
  --max-context-length 128000 \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126 --num-dataset-entries 393 \
  --concurrency 32 --streaming --use-server-token-count \
  --trajectory-start-min-ratio 0.25 --trajectory-start-max-ratio 0.75 \
  --benchmark-duration 1800 --agentic-cache-warmup-duration 600 --warmup-grace-period 1800 \
  --failed-request-threshold 0.10 --random-seed 42 \
  --output-artifact-dir /results

# Run as a Job; results land on the benchmark-results PVC. Allow ~2 h.
oc apply -f benchmarks/manifests/aiperf-agentx-128k-job.yaml -n ${NAMESPACE}
oc wait --for=condition=complete job/aiperf-agentx-128k -n ${NAMESPACE} --timeout=2h
harness_drawer.name: aiperf-agentx-128k-job.yaml

benchmark.harness_lede: AIPerf (ai-dynamo/aiperf) replays the date-pinned AgentX corpus — 393 multi-turn, long-context coding traces — with the inferencex-agentx-mvp scenario. This is the shared workload in benchmarks/manifests/, so results compare across models. Use the 128K variant only because this recipe serves 131K; the unlimited-context variant would count every overflow as a failure.
notes: Real agentic sessions overflow 131K. In the Weka trace replay, 42 of 50 sessions exceeded the context window.
benchmark.provenance: Pending run — AIPerf AgentX 128K benchmark has not been executed for this recipe yet. The row below is a placeholder for the expected workload shape.

configure.flags_lede: Ten flags plus two common. Each is load-bearing for agentic serving at 131K — drop any of the four parser and tool flags and tool calling silently degrades to prose.

flags_rows.why: One node, eight GPUs, no cross-node transport.
~16% throughput uplift over GLM-5 on the same topology. The main reason this profile holds 131K.
The model's context window. Real agent sessions still overflow it — 42 of 50 in the trace replay.
63% lower TTFT p50 on shared-prefix traffic. Cheapest win in this file.
Keeps a long prefill from starving in-flight decodes.
GLM-5.2 ships an MTP head. Free decode speedup — and it disappears under pipeline parallelism.
The head predicts five. Raising it costs verification compute for falling acceptance.
Required for structured tool arguments. Without it you get prose.
Separates reasoning from content. The chat template also honors enable_thinking and reasoning_effort.
Lets the model decide when to call. Omit it and the parser never fires.
Stable client-facing name, decoupled from the checkpoint path.
The GlmMoeDsa architecture requires it.

manifest.body:
# GLM-5.2 on H200 — aggregated, single node, TP=8.
# Profile: AIPerf AgentX 128K (131K · tools · MTP)
# Checkpoint: zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8
#
# Note: RHOAI 3.5 LLMInferenceServiceConfigs do not include a
# pipeline-parallel template; PP=2 needs a custom config first.
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha2
kind: LLMInferenceService
metadata:
  name: glm52
spec:
  model:
    uri: pvc://glm52-weights
    name: glm-5.2-fp8
  replicas: 1
  parallelism:
    tensor: 8
  template:
    containers:
      - name: main
        image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.24.0
        env:
          - name: HF_TOKEN
            valueFrom:
              secretKeyRef: { name: llm-d-hf-token, key: HF_TOKEN, optional: true }
          - name: VLLM_ADDITIONAL_ARGS
            value: >-
              --tensor-parallel-size 8
              --kv-cache-dtype fp8
              --max-model-len 131072
              --enable-prefix-caching
              --enable-chunked-prefill
              --speculative-config.method mtp
              --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 5
              --tool-call-parser glm47
              --reasoning-parser glm45
              --enable-auto-tool-choice
              --served-model-name glm-5.2-fp8
              --trust-remote-code
        resources:
          requests: { cpu: 32, memory: 512Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: "8" }
          limits: { memory: 512Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: "8" }
        startupProbe:
          httpGet: { path: /health, port: 8000 }
          failureThreshold: 180
          periodSeconds: 10
        volumeMounts: [{ name: dshm, mountPath: /dev/shm }]
    volumes: [{ name: dshm, emptyDir: { medium: Memory, sizeLimit: 16Gi } }]
manifest.name: llmisvc-h200-single-agentic.yaml

configure.vllm_serve:
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 131072 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --speculative-config.method mtp \
  --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 5 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --served-model-name glm-5.2-fp8 \
  --trust-remote-code

harness_drawer.code:
guidellm benchmark \
  --target "http://${SERVICE}:8000" \
  --data "prompt_tokens=8000,output_tokens=1000" \
  --rate-type "concurrent" \
  --rate "1,4,16" \
  --backend-type "openai_http" \
  --model "zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8" \
  --max-seconds "300" \
  --output-path "output_vllm_glm52_spec.json"

# Version pin required: guidellm==0.3.0 (CLI form removed in 0.7+)
harness_drawer.name: guidellm-8k1k-sweep.sh

benchmark.harness_lede: GuideLLM against a fixed 8000/1000 shape, 300 s per stage. The command runs a 1 → 4 → 16 concurrency sweep, but only the C=16 stage has a committed result run and is reported below. This matches the internal performance-team standard, so the point is comparable across models.
notes: Prefix caching is the cheapest win available. Shared-prefix traffic showed 63% lower TTFT p50 and 12% higher throughput, with no external infrastructure.
benchmark.provenance: Only the C=16 point is published here. It is the single normalized result traced to a committed result run (results/guidellm-8k1k-c16-r1/). The harness command below still runs the full 1 → 4 → 16 sweep, but the C=1 and C=4 stages are not yet backed by a committed result run, so they are not published. Re-run and commit results before quoting any lower-concurrency number, and re-verify before any external claim.

configure.arg_note: Two deliberate omissions against the agentic profile: no --kv-cache-dtype fp8 (KV pressure is low at 10K, and auto dtype sidesteps any quantization effect on quality), and no parsers (this profile targets completion-style serving). Add --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice if you need tools.
configure.flags_lede: Eight flags plus two common, tuned for density rather than reach. The context ceiling is the price: --max-model-len 10000 rejects anything longer, so never point agentic traffic here.

flags_rows.why: One node, eight GPUs.
8K in + 1K out + margin. Small per-sequence KV means more concurrent sequences fit. Any longer request is rejected — that is the trade.
Caps the scheduler batch. Keeps ITL flat at C=16 with room for MTP verification.
Deliberately conservative. Leaves HBM for draft KV and CUDA graph pools; at 10K max-len you do not need 0.90.
With the batched-token cap below, an 8K prompt prefills in one chunk.
One prompt, one chunk, no queueing behind decodes. This is why TTFT p50 stays near 0.7 s.
48 sequences × 6 MTP draft slots. Move max-num-seqs and this must move with it.
Draft TP must be 1 or the target TP. At TP=8, 8.
Stable client-facing name, decoupled from the checkpoint path.
The GlmMoeDsa architecture requires it.

manifest.body:
# GLM-5.2 on H200 — aggregated, single node, TP=8.
# Profile: GuideLLM 8K/1K (8K in · 1K out)
# Checkpoint: zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8
#
# Note: RHOAI 3.5 LLMInferenceServiceConfigs do not include a
# pipeline-parallel template; PP=2 needs a custom config first.
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha2
kind: LLMInferenceService
metadata:
  name: glm52
spec:
  model:
    uri: pvc://glm52-weights
    name: glm-5.2-fp8
  replicas: 1
  parallelism:
    tensor: 8
  template:
    containers:
      - name: main
        image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.24.0
        env:
          - name: HF_TOKEN
            valueFrom:
              secretKeyRef: { name: llm-d-hf-token, key: HF_TOKEN, optional: true }
          - name: VLLM_ADDITIONAL_ARGS
            value: >-
              --tensor-parallel-size 8
              --max-model-len 10000
              --max-num-seqs 48
              --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80
              --enable-chunked-prefill
              --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
              --max-cudagraph-capture-size 192
              --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_tensor_parallel_size":8}'
              --served-model-name glm-5.2-fp8
              --trust-remote-code
        resources:
          requests: { cpu: 32, memory: 512Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: "8" }
          limits: { memory: 512Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: "8" }
        startupProbe:
          httpGet: { path: /health, port: 8000 }
          failureThreshold: 180
          periodSeconds: 10
        volumeMounts: [{ name: dshm, mountPath: /dev/shm }]
    volumes: [{ name: dshm, emptyDir: { medium: Memory, sizeLimit: 16Gi } }]
manifest.name: llmisvc-h200-single-throughput.yaml
